transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?
Lately I keep hearing this voice telling me my heart is going to give out and that it’s already too late for me. It sounds so real, and it just won't leave me alone.
How long have you been hearing this voice, and did it start suddenly over a few days or has it been going on for months or longer?

I've been hearing that voice for about four months now. It didn't just start out of nowhere; it began a few weeks after the cardiologist diagnosed me, once I had already sunk into this really deep, dark sadness.
When you are not feeling sad, do you still hear the voice or believe your heart is definitely failing, or do those experiences only happen when your mood is very low?

I never heard that voice or believed my heart was doomed before I fell into this deep depression. It only started happening after I sank into this dark spell where just getting out of bed and caring about anything felt completely impossible.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were [F20.0, F23.1, F22.0], but the new history makes a primary psychotic disorder less likely because the voice and heart-failure belief began only after the onset of a severe depressive episode and appear mood-congruent. This pattern argues against a schizophrenia-spectrum or persistent delusional disorder and instead supports a depressive episode with psychotic features, so the current candidate list is narrowed to the depressive psychosis code.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a depressive episode with severe low mood, marked loss of motivation/energy, and mood-congruent psychotic symptoms (a voice saying his heart will fail and he is doomed). The psychotic experience began only after the depressive episode started and occurs in the context of the depression, supporting severe depressive episode with psychotic symptoms.
